newsitem.title: USA: Seagate sees weak results, market share erodes.
newsitem.headline: Seagate sees weak results, market share erodes.

text.p: Seagate Technology Inc., one of the largest U.S. makers of computer disk drives, warned Monday its fiscal fourth quarter results would be below expectations due to weak demand for its high-performance computer disk drive products.

Chairman, President and Chief Executive Al Shugard said in an interview that the weak demand was restricted to the high-end of the market for file servers, where Seagate is losing market share, and not in the personal computer market.

"We've seen some softening ... it was across the board, it's a general kind of slowness," Shugard said, adding that in the desk-top market "there is more demand (for disk-drives) than we have supply."
Technology stocks have been volatile in recent weeks on concerns that demand for personal computers is slowing.

In a brief statement issued after markets closed, Seagate said revenues for the three months ended in June are expected to be between 6 percent and 10 percent below the $2.5 billion reported for the third quarter ended in March. The company also said earnings before one-time charges could fall short of the third quarter's profit of $1.01 a share.
Wall Street analysts had expected the company to earn $1.06 a share in its fiscal fourth quarter, according to the First Call service.
In the year-ago quarter, Seagate earned $101 million, or 92 cents a primary share, on revenues of $2.01 billion.

"We may be losing a little market share in the high end," Shugard said. He said Seagate was not losing "a significant amount" of market share but that new entrants such as International Business Machines Corp., Quantum Corp. and Western Digital Corp. were eating away at Seagate's business. Seagate has about 60 percent of the high end market.
Kimball Brown, a Dataquest Inc. analyst, also said he has seen no sign of a slowdown in demand for personal computers.
"In no case have we seen a general slowdown, there is demand for boxes, it's just a mix shift," Brown said.

Shares of the Scotts Valley, Calif.-based disk drive maker have been under pressure in recent days on concerns about a possible oversupply in the global disk-drive market. Last week, a Singapore newspaper reported Seagate may have to cut its high-end output in Singapore and that May and June production levels could be as much as 30 percent below March levels.
Shugard dismissed those reports as misleading, adding that rumors the company may be cutting staff were also inaccurate.
"The reports out of Singapore were inaccurate," he said.
Shugard said the long-term outlook for the storage business remains strong. "The data storage business long-term, the potential is outstanding," he said.

Separately, Seagate said it will seek authorization from its board of directors to repurchase up to an additional $600 million worth of its stock. This is in addition to the nearly $570 million of its stock purchased during the current fiscal year. At the end of its third quarter, Seagate had about 255.3 million shares outstanding.
Earlier, Segate shares closed at $42.375, up $1.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
